papers.title: The DYNAM-O Toolbox: Characterizing Individualized Neural Signatures in Sleep EEG
papers.summary: This paper introduces the DYNAM-O Toolbox, an open-source software for data-driven characterization of transient oscillations in sleep EEG using a multi-resolution time-frequency peak detection method. Analysis of overnight EEG from 133 adults revealed sex differences in fast-spindle center frequency and low-alpha activity, demonstrating its utility for group-level inference.

papers.title: ViSTA-SleepNet: A View-Integrated and Subject-Adaptive Transformer Framework for Multimodal Sleep Staging.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: ViSTA-SleepNet, a two-stage transformer framework, integrates multi-view EEG, EOG, and EMG features with demographic adaptation for sleep staging, achieving 88.5%, 84.5%, and 89.6% accuracy on Sleep-EDF-20, Sleep-EDF-78, and SHHS, with >95% accuracy in spindle and slow-wave detection.

papers.title: Tilia Tomentosa promotes sleep, preserving sleep structure.
papers.summary: In freely moving mice, chronic treatment with Tilia tomentosa extract increased NREM sleep during the active period, reduced wakefulness, and decreased brief awakenings during resting hours without altering overall sleep structure or EEG spectral features. These findings support Tilia's sleep-promoting and sleep-stabilizing effects.

papers.title: SEDAT: A hybrid tokenizer for large EEG models.
papers.summary: This paper introduces SEDAT, a hybrid tokenizer for large EEG foundation models, integrating spatial aggregation, data-adaptive filtering, and adaptive segmentation. It achieves classification improvements up to 15.3% over fixed-length windowing across ten heterogeneous EEG datasets.

papers.title: AVOCODO: An open-source multimodal annotation platform for developmental EEG
papers.summary: This paper presents AVOCODO, an open-source MATLAB platform that integrates synchronized behavioral annotation of video with EEG recordings from EGI MFF files. It has been applied in five developmental EEG studies with over 500 pediatric participants, improving efficiency and reproducibility of behavioral coding.

papers.title: Wide-Field Ca2+ Imaging Reveals Cortical Dynamics Across Propofol Anesthesia and Emergence in Adult Mice.
papers.summary: Wide-field Ca2+ imaging in mice reveals that propofol anesthesia suppresses cortical activity, and after emergence, local activity recovers but inter-regional functional connectivity remains below baseline for at least 1.5 hours, indicating a dissociation between local and network-level recovery.

papers.title: In-home validation of wrist actigraphy against portable electroencephalography for sleep assessment in older adults.
papers.summary: In 49 community-dwelling older adults over 217 nights, wrist actigraphy versus portable EEG showed acceptable accuracy for average total sleep time (ICC=0.73, MAPE=11%) but poor accuracy for sleep onset latency and wake after sleep onset (MAPE>50%). Actigraphy is suitable for estimating average sleep duration but not for sleep fragmentation indices in this population.

papers.title: Application of Machine Learning Models to Identify Differences in Neural Electrophysiological Properties Across Estrous Cycle Phases.
papers.summary: Machine learning models, including Random Forest, classified estrous cycle phase from nucleus accumbens neuron electrophysiology with up to 94% accuracy, with late proestrus as the most distinct phase, demonstrating MLMs can detect subtle neuromodulatory changes.

papers.title: A fused minimum spanning tree framework reveals large-scale cortical network reorganization during dual-task standing in older adults.
papers.summary: This study used EEG functional connectivity and minimum spanning tree (MST) topology to examine cortical network reorganization during dual-task standing in older adults, finding increased postural sway and altered network topology with dual-task conditions. A novel fused MST framework integrating multiple frequency bands provided a more integrated characterization of network adaptation than band-specific MST.

papers.title: U2Multi-UDA: A Unified Multilevel Multisource Unsupervised Domain Adaptation Method for Motor Imagery.
papers.journal: IEEE transactions on neural networks and learning systems
papers.summary: U2Multi-UDA is a unified multilevel multisource unsupervised domain adaptation framework for motor imagery decoding, integrating optimal transport, cross-attention, and low-rank adaptation, improving mean accuracy on three datasets by up to 3.83 percentage points over baselines.

papers.title: EEG-VID: Task-Guided Latent Predictive Pretraining for EEG Decoding and Assistive Target Selection
papers.summary: EEG-VID is a pretraining framework that predicts future EEG states with task guidance, improving decoding accuracy across VIG-48 and BCI Competition datasets in most comparisons (41/42). In a robot-scene study, it achieved 40.24% accuracy for target selection versus 25% chance, supporting its use for assistive applications.

papers.title: Averaged sparse local representation for the elimination of pseudo-HFOs from intracranial EEG recording in epilepsy.
papers.journal: International IEEE/EMBS Conference on Neural Engineering : [proceedings]. International IEEE EMBS Conference on Neural Engineering
papers.summary: This study proposes a sparse representation framework combined with a random forest classifier to distinguish real HFOs from pseudo-HFOs in intracranial EEG. The method achieved 89.77% classification accuracy on labeled events and significantly improved seizure onset zone localization by 18.27% compared to conventional amplitude-threshold-based detection.

papers.title: EEG-AS: Instance-Level Foundation Model Selection for EEG Foundation Models via Behavior Reconstruction
papers.summary: This paper introduces EEG-AS, an instance-level algorithm selection framework for EEG foundation models that reconstructs the behaviors of multiple foundation models from inference-available features to select the best model for each EEG instance. Experiments on seven public benchmarks show that EEG-AS substantially narrows the gap between the single best solver and the oracle upper bound.

papers.title: Centrifugal Effects of Voluntary Movements on Somatosensory and Auditory Evoked Potentials: An Exploratory Study.
papers.summary: This exploratory study compared centrifugal modulation of somatosensory and auditory evoked potentials during voluntary movement, attention, and passive conditions. They found that movement increased P100, N140, and N1 amplitudes compared to attention/passive conditions, with larger positive difference waveform components for somatosensory than auditory, suggesting modality-specific centrifugal effects.

papers.title: Integrating Spatial-Temporal Channel Reliability with AI for Robust High-Frequency Oscillation Detection in Intracranial EEG.
papers.journal: International IEEE/EMBS Conference on Neural Engineering : [proceedings]. International IEEE EMBS Conference on Neural Engineering
papers.summary: This paper presents a reliability-guided HFO analysis pipeline integrating event-level denoising, channel signal quality assessment, and temporal reliability analysis for intracranial EEG. Applying the pipeline improved SOZ localization accuracy from 66% to 93%, demonstrating that spatial and temporal context improves HFO artifact rejection and clinical specificity.

papers.title: Contrastive Decoupling and Enhancement of Multi-view EEG Features for Imagined Speech Decoding.
papers.summary: MFCDE framework extracts and decouples multi-view EEG features (temporal, spectral, PLV, graph) for imagined speech decoding, outperforming baselines and revealing complementary neural dynamics for speech discrimination.

papers.title: EEG microstate reconfiguration across cognitive states in preschool children with developmental language disorder.
papers.summary: This study compared EEG microstate organization across rest, semantic matching, and auditory oddball tasks in preschool children with and without developmental language disorder (DLD). While microstate features varied across task contexts, no robust group differences in conventional microstate features or transition probabilities survived correction, suggesting limited evidence for DLD-specific alterations in this sample.

papers.title: Prioritization in working memory reduces interference via beta band-linked stimulus transformations.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.summary: This study used behavioral and EEG experiments in humans to examine prioritization in working memory with a two-step retrocuing task. Results showed that prioritized items are shielded from interference, and this shielding may be implemented by transforming the unprioritized item into a state maintained by a mechanism cycling at ~15 Hz (low-beta), distinct from beta-bursting.

papers.title: Multi-Task EEG Diffusion Framework for Motor Functional Recovery in Stroke Patients.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: The authors propose a unified EEG-based framework using a diffusion model with decoupled neural architecture and rotary spatial encoding for motor imagery classification, hemiplegic side detection, and functional recovery prediction in stroke patients. The method shows superior performance and generalizability across multiple MI-BCI tasks, supporting its potential for personalized stroke rehabilitation.

papers.title: Prognostic Significance of EEG Patterns in Post-Cardiac Arrest Coma: A Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study of 1,000 Patients.
papers.summary: This multicenter retrospective cohort study of 1,000 comatose patients after cardiac arrest quantified the prognostic value of EEG patterns for poor outcome. Flat EEG had a positive predictive value (PPO) of 1.00, status epilepticus had PPO up to 1.00, but suppression had PPO 0.76-0.83 with a false-positive rate of 17-24%, highlighting variable prognostic uncertainty over time.

papers.title: Meditation styles are highly discriminable from EEG at the subject level with limited generalization across the population: a machine-learning study.
papers.summary: This study assessed whether EEG-based machine learning can classify three meditation styles (Shamatha, Vipassana, Metta) and mind-wandering in experienced meditators. It found high intra-subject accuracy but much lower inter-subject generalization, indicating subject-specific neural signatures and challenges for subject-independent classification.

papers.title: Profiles of Anxiety in Children Undergoing Elective Surgery: Predictors and Perioperative Outcomes.
papers.summary: The study identified two latent profiles of preoperative anxiety in 171 children undergoing elective surgery: average (74%) and heightened (26%). Children with heightened anxiety had higher shyness, more distress behaviors in the operating room, and tended to have higher postoperative pain.

papers.title: Impaired midfrontal‑motor theta phase synchronization characterizes maladaptive motivational behavior in people with obsessive‑compulsive disorder.
papers.summary: This study investigates maladaptive motivational behavior in OCD using a motivational Go/NoGo learning task with computational modeling and EEG. They found that people with OCD show stronger Pavlovian bias and lower learning rates, with conflict-related theta enhancement emerging too late to influence choice, and midfrontal-motor theta phase synchrony failing to modulate motivational biases, suggesting a neural mechanism for insight-action dissociation.

papers.title: CREST: A Cortical Resting-State EEG Spatial Transformer for Chronic Pain Inference
papers.summary: This paper introduces CREST, a spatial transformer that uses resting-state EEG spectrograms from 56 cortical regions to classify chronic pain status. In a study of 125 people, it achieved an AUROC of 0.782 (permutation p<0.005), with control experiments implicating individual alpha rhythms.

papers.title: Characteristics of sustained attention impairment in individuals under simulated positive acceleration stress: separation effect of early and late stage cognitive processing.
papers.summary: This study investigated sustained attention impairment under simulated positive acceleration stress using lower body negative pressure and EEG. Results showed a dissociation between early and late processing stages, with reduced P2 latency (enhanced early perceptual processing) and reduced P300 amplitude (impaired late response selection), suggesting adaptive compensation.

papers.title: Midbrain Glutamatergic Neurons Modulate the Acoustic Startle Reflex and Prepulse Inhibition in Mice.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.summary: This study examined the role of pedunculopontine tegmental nucleus (PPTg) glutamatergic neurons in acoustic startle and prepulse inhibition (PPI) in mice. Optogenetic inhibition of PPTg-PnC glutamatergic synapses increased PPI without altering baseline startle, while activation modulated startle in a time-dependent manner, identifying a novel excitatory mechanism in sensorimotor gating.

papers.title: From form to concept: a dynamic spatiotemporal brain network cascade supports language comprehension.
papers.summary: Using EEG-fMRI fusion in healthy adults, the authors introduce the Form-to-Concept framework, identifying a sequence of brain network activations from perceptual word processing to concept coherence across time windows. The framework reveals that canonical ERP components reflect a temporally structured cascade of distributed networks, with stronger comprehension associated with enhanced mid-to-late inferential processes.

papers.title: Distinct Neural Dynamics Underlying Reward Expectation Formation and Outcome Processing: Insights From ERP and Time-Frequency Analyses.
papers.summary: This EEG study separated reward expectation formation from outcome processing in a two-stage binary-choice task and found distinct neural dynamics: RewP-latency measures were larger for certain outcomes, P3b-latency measures increased for certain losses, and RewP-theta was the earliest marker of sensitivity to certain losses, while at outcome, RewP and P3b were larger for unexpected wins. The results highlight the importance of distinguishing expectation formation from outcome phases and the value of multimethodological analyses in reward-based decision-making.

papers.title: Investigation of the predictive value of routine electroencephalogram compared to continuous electroencephalogram in the acute phase of traumatic brain injury.
papers.summary: This prospective study of 35 adults with acute traumatic brain injury compared routine, 1-hour, and continuous EEG for detecting epileptiform activity. Prolonged EEG increased detection of interictal epileptiform discharges and identified an electrographic seizure missed by shorter recordings, though clinical variables may help prioritize patients for shorter monitoring.

papers.title: Integrating socioeconomic context with multimodal EEG data for improved ADHD risk screening.
papers.summary: This study introduces a multimodal deep learning architecture that integrates temporal EEG, spectro-temporal patterns, and socioeconomic context for ADHD risk screening. The multimodal model outperformed EEG-only baselines on epoch-level accuracy and sensitivity, and in leave-one-subject-out cross-validation achieved accuracy 0.92-0.96, though McNemar's test did not reach significance.

papers.title: Gastrodia elata Blume and Acorus tatarinowii Schott mixtures alleviate pentylenetetrazol-induced seizures in mice: association with NLRP3 inflammasome signaling changes.
papers.journal: The Journal of pharmacy and pharmacology
papers.summary: The study evaluated the anti-seizure effects of the Gastrodia elata-Acorus tatarinowii herb pair in mouse models of epilepsy. It reduced seizure severity, improved cognitive function, and modulated NLRP3/caspase-1/IL-1β pathway, suggesting multi-target anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective mechanisms.

papers.title: Electroencephalography-Based Measures to Understand Meditation and Mindfulness: Bibliometric Scoping Review of Randomized Controlled Trials.
papers.journal: Global advances in integrative medicine and health
papers.summary: This bibliometric scoping review summarized 142 randomized controlled trials using EEG-based measures to assess meditation and mindfulness interventions. It found significant heterogeneity in study populations, designs, and outcomes, and determined that further systematic reviews require more original studies.

papers.title: Reinstatement of escitalopram and clonidine administration reverses the cessation-induced enhanced activation of rat norepinephrine and serotonin neuronal firing activity.
papers.summary: The study used in vivo electrophysiology in male rats to show that abrupt cessation of escitalopram, a serotonin reuptake inhibitor, increased firing of norepinephrine and serotonin neurons, and that acute re-injection of escitalopram or clonidine reversed this overactivation.

papers.title: An eikonal model with re-excitability for fast simulations in cardiac electrophysiology.
papers.summary: The authors extended the eikonal model to include tissue re-excitability, allowing simulation of re-entrant cardiac arrhythmias. The model reproduced anisotropic conduction and action potential duration with qualitative accuracy in macro-reentry cases while being computationally efficient for clinical digital twin applications.

papers.title: The Efficacy of Therapies for Phantom Limb Pain in Amputees Assessed via Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI) and Electroencephalography (EEG) Measures of Cortical Reorganization: A Scoping Review.
papers.summary: This scoping review assessed nonpharmacologic therapies for phantom limb pain using fMRI and EEG measures of cortical reorganization. Most effective therapies were associated with changes in sensorimotor cortex organization, but the relationship between cortical changes and pain reduction was inconsistent, suggesting a multifactorial network-level condition.

papers.title: Status Epilepticus and Lateralized Periodic Discharges (LPDs) in Cannabis Withdrawal Syndrome: A Case Report and Review of the Literature.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 53-year-old woman who developed tonic-clonic status epilepticus and lateralized periodic discharges after abrupt cannabis withdrawal. Treatment with anticonvulsants led to clinical improvement and resolution of EEG abnormalities, highlighting the need for anticonvulsant treatment in such cases.

papers.title: High-order harmonic generation from an atom in a disordered environment.
papers.summary: Through one-dimensional simulations with open quantum systems, the study shows that in high-order harmonic generation from an atom in a disordered environment, local dephasing of the photoelectron wavepacket leads to global decoherence and a quantum-to-classical transition, manifesting as quantum scars in real-time dynamics.

papers.title: Broadband microwave time-frequency analysis via stabilized period-one oscillation and recirculating frequency shifting with a shared fiber loop.
papers.summary: The authors propose a broadband microwave time-frequency analysis method using stabilized period-one oscillation and recirculating frequency shifting with a shared fiber loop. They experimentally demonstrated an instantaneous analysis bandwidth of up to 57 GHz, a frequency resolution of 60 MHz, and a maximum mean absolute frequency measurement error of 38.16 MHz.

papers.title: Preparation of Plasma Membrane Vesicles, Lysosomes, Proteoliposomes and Alternative Sample Types for SSM-Based Electrophysiology.
papers.summary: This chapter provides a detailed protocol for preparing plasma membrane vesicles and lysosomes from mammalian cell culture for SSM-based electrophysiology, using nitrogen decompression and sucrose gradient centrifugation. It also covers alternative sample types and preparation strategies, including proteoliposomes, and reports enrichment of 14 marker proteins to evaluate purity.

papers.title: Safety and Feasibility of Deep Sedation With a Tulip Airway and Jaw Elevation Device During Electrophysiology Procedures: A Single-Center Experience of 647 Consecutive Cases.
papers.summary: This single-center retrospective study evaluated the safety and feasibility of deep sedation with a Tulip airway and jaw elevation device in 647 patients undergoing electrophysiology procedures. All procedures were completed without sedation discontinuation, with one intubation (0.2%) and three procedure-related complications (0.5%), indicating safety in selected lower-risk patients.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
